chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) gave the grandfather one-sixth as a sustenance share.' It is upon the understanding that the sustenance share is only for the grandfather or the grandmother if their child is alive; as for when that child is absent, they do not have a sustenance share either, in a state which indicates that what was narrated:

key_terms.طُعْمَة: Sustenance share (a specific type of inheritance portion)
key_terms.وَلَدُهُمَا: Their child (the parent of the deceased)

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of a grandfather in Shia fiqh and under what conditions does he receive it?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the status of the grandfather (al-jadd) as a residuary heir who receives one-sixth as a 'sustenance share' (tu'mah) only when his direct child (the parent of the deceased) is alive, illustrating the Shia principle of 'blocking' (hajb) by closer degrees. It highlights the scholarly distinction between the grandfather's share as a fixed portion versus a residuary allocation, depending on the presence of intermediate heirs.
